name: Japan
shape: automatic loss on voluntary acquisition; separate election requirement at majority for those dual from birth
instrument: 国籍法 (Nationality Act), Act No. 147 of 4 May 1950
quote_original: 日本国民は、自己の志望によつて外国の国籍を取得したときは、日本の国籍を失う。
quote_translation: A Japanese national loses Japanese nationality when he or she acquires a foreign nationality by his or her own volition.
asymmetry_note: Not birth-vs-naturalised in the usual sense, but two materially different regimes. Art. 11(1) strips an existing Japanese national who naturalises abroad, by operation of law, with no application or decision. Art. 14 instead imposes an election duty on people who hold Japanese and foreign nationality from birth (by age 20 where both were held before 18, otherwise within two years), and its sanction under art. 15(3) only bites one month after a ministerial demand. Art. 16(1) then requires only that a person who has declared election 外国の国籍の離脱に努めなければならない, that is, shall endeavour to renounce the foreign nationality. That is an obligation of effort, not a loss rule.
notes: The human-readable page at https://laws.e-gov.go.jp/law/325AC0000000147 is an SPA shell of about 800 bytes and contains no article text; quotes will not verify against it. The /api/ URL above returns the full consolidated XML (61,679 bytes on 9 Aug 2026) and the quote was byte-checked against those bytes. e-Gov serves the current text by default; the XML carries no explicit consolidation date, so no consolidation date is asserted here. Art. 14's age thresholds reflect the 2022 civil-majority amendment. Recorded prohibited rather than conditional because the direction in which that errs is the safe one: it tells a user considering naturalisation abroad the true thing. See asymmetry_note before publishing anything about people dual from birth.

name: China
shape: non-recognition of dual status plus automatic loss on voluntary acquisition
instrument: Nationality Law of the People's Republic of China, adopted at the Third Session of the Fifth National People's Congress, promulgated by Order No. 8 and effective 10 September 1980
quote_original: The People's Republic of China does not recognize dual nationality for any Chinese national.
quote_translation: (source is the official NPC English text; no translation required)
asymmetry_note: No birth-versus-naturalised split. There is instead a residence element that comparative tables routinely drop: art. 9 loss is drafted as applying to a Chinese national "who has settled abroad and who has been naturalized as a foreign national or has acquired foreign nationality of his own free will". On the face of the text settlement abroad is a conjunctive element of the rule, not colour. Flagged as a live ambiguity, not asserted as a carve-out.
notes: Apostrophe in the quote is a straight ASCII apostrophe exactly as served by npc.gov.cn; do not normalise it to a typographic apostrophe or the check will fail. Art. 8: a person whose application for naturalisation as a Chinese national has been approved "shall not retain foreign nationality". Art. 9: such a person "shall automatically lose Chinese nationality". Source is the official National People's Congress English translation. The Chinese original was not obtained: the npc.gov.cn and gov.cn Chinese-language URLs tried both 404'd.

name: India
instrument: The Citizenship Act, 1955 (Act No. 57 of 1955), consolidated text "[As on the 15th April, 2026]"
quote_original: voluntarily acquired, the citizenship of another country shall, upon such acquisition or, as the
quote_translation: (source is in English; no translation required)
asymmetry_note: Section 9(1) applies to "Any citizen of India" without distinguishing how citizenship was acquired.
notes: quote_original is the line-safe form: it is a single unbroken line in the PDF. The full clause, which spans a PDF line break, reads "voluntarily acquired, the citizenship of another country shall, upon such acquisition or, as the case may be, such commencement, cease to be a citizen of India". Do not quote the opening of s. 9(1): pdftotext renders it as "by naturalisation, registration otherwise voluntarily acquires", dropping the "or", in both -layout and raw modes. The only qualification in the sub-section suspends the rule for acquisitions during a war in which India is engaged, until the Central Government directs otherwise. Overseas Citizen of India (ss. 7A-7B) is a separate registration status and is not citizenship; those sections were not read in full. Only the outbound direction is established here; the inbound naturalisation requirement was not read.

name: Malaysia
shape: permission and discretion regime, not automatic loss
instrument: Federal Constitution of Malaysia, reprint as at 30 November 2025
quote_original: formal act (other than marriage) the citizenship of any country
quote_translation: (source is the official English text; no translation required)
asymmetry_note: Art. 24(1) is drafted as applying to "any citizen", with no birth-versus-registration distinction on its face.
notes: This is the most commonly mis-stated row in the set. Art. 24(1) provides that where the Federal Government is satisfied a citizen has acquired foreign citizenship by registration, naturalisation or other voluntary and formal act other than marriage, it "may by order deprive that person of his citizenship". That is a discretionary executive power exercised under the art. 27 procedure. Nothing happens by operation of law, which is the whole practical difference from the Japan-shaped rule Malaysia is usually grouped with. Art. 24(2) gives the same discretionary power where a citizen has voluntarily claimed and exercised rights accorded exclusively to citizens of another country. RETRIEVAL WARNING: the landing page https://lom.agc.gov.my/federal-constitution.php embeds pdf.js and hides the file behind viewer.html?file=..., the same shape as the Gibraltar viewerjs trap. The filename contains a Unicode Private Use Area character U+F022, encoded %EF%80%A2, between "WJW25" and "0908". The visually obvious URL without it returns nginx HTTP 500. The byte-exact URL in source_url is the one that works. The reprint carries the footnote "*This Article has been amended by section 7 of the Constitution (Amendment) Act 2025 [Act A1752], not yet in force." The amendments detailed in the notes affect art. 23 (renunciation); re-check art. 24 before Act A1752 commences.

name: Austria
shape: automatic loss on voluntary acquisition unless prior retention permission (permission regime)
instrument: Staatsbürgerschaftsgesetz 1985, consolidated federal law, page header states Fassung vom 09.08.2026
articles: sec. 27(1); retention at sec. 28(1)-(3); extension to children at sec. 29; naturalisation assurance at sec. 20(1)
quote_original: Die Staatsbürgerschaft verliert, wer auf Grund seines Antrages, seiner Erklärung oder seiner ausdrücklichen Zustimmung eine fremde Staatsangehörigkeit erwirbt
quote_translation: A person loses citizenship who, on the basis of his application, his declaration or his express consent, acquires a foreign nationality.
asymmetry_note: Yes, but only in the retention route. Sec. 28(2) opens the private-and-family-life ground for retention exclusively to citizens who acquired citizenship by descent ("wenn sie die Staatsbürgerschaft durch Abstammung erworben haben"). Everyone else must qualify under sec. 28(1), which requires that retention be in the interest of the Republic on account of services rendered or a particularly worthy ground, and, where reciprocity exists, the consent of the other state.
notes: Section-sign characters are deliberately absent from quote_original. RIS's GeltendeFassung view renders each sentence twice, once with abbreviations and once with them expanded ("§ 27" alongside "Paragraph 27,"), so any quote containing a section sign is fragile against this host. Sec. 28(3) requires a written application and makes the retention permission conditional on the foreign nationality being acquired within two years. Inbound direction established from sec. 20(1): naturalisation is first only assured, conditional on the applicant proving exit from his previous state within two years.

name: Netherlands
shape: automatic loss on voluntary acquisition with three named exceptions, plus long-absence loss
instrument: Rijkswet op het Nederlanderschap, consolidated version in force from 1 October 2023
articles: art. 15(1)(a), art. 15(1)(c), art. 15(2), art. 15(4); inbound at art. 9(1)(b) and art. 9(3)
quote_original: door het vrijwillig verkrijgen van een andere nationaliteit
quote_translation: by the voluntary acquisition of another nationality
asymmetry_note: No birth-versus-naturalised split in art. 15(1)(a) itself. The exceptions in art. 15(2) turn on facts about the person's connection to the other country, not on how Dutch nationality was acquired: born in the country of the other nationality and principally resident there at the time of acquisition; principally resident there for at least five uninterrupted years before majority; or married to a holder of that nationality.
notes: The bare URL https://wetten.overheid.nl/BWBR0003738/ redirects to the dated URL above, which is the version in force. AMENDMENT WATCH: the art. 15 block carries the banner "Toekomstige wijziging(en) voorzien met ingang van: 01-03-2027." A future amendment is scheduled for 1 March 2027; re-check before then. Art. 15(1)(c) is a separate and easily missed trap: loss after thirteen uninterrupted years of principal residence outside the Kingdom and outside the EU while holding both nationalities, a period art. 15(4) restarts on issue of a Dutch passport, identity card or certificate of nationality. Inbound: art. 9(1)(b) refuses naturalisation to an applicant who has not done what is possible to lose the other nationality, and art. 9(3) exempts nationals of Second Protocol states, applicants born and principally resident in the Kingdom, spouses of Dutch nationals, and recognised refugees.

name: Spain
shape: designated-country list, on both the loss limb and the renunciation limb
instrument: Código Civil, BOE consolidated text; art. 24 last modified by Ley 36/2002, art. 23 last modified by Ley 12/2015
quote_original: La adquisición de la nacionalidad de países iberoamericanos, Andorra, Filipinas, Guinea Ecuatorial o Portugal no es bastante para producir, conforme a este apartado, la pérdida de la nacionalidad española de origen.
quote_translation: Acquisition of the nationality of Ibero-American countries, Andorra, the Philippines, Equatorial Guinea or Portugal is not sufficient to produce, under this paragraph, the loss of Spanish nationality of origin.
asymmetry_note: Yes, and it is textual rather than inferred. The art. 24.1 carve-out is expressed as protecting "la nacionalidad española de origen", nationality OF ORIGIN. On its face it does not protect a naturalised Spaniard who later acquires, say, Colombian nationality. A single status value cannot carry a Spaniard by origin and a naturalised Spaniard under different rules.
notes: Confirms the brief's hypothesis that Spain is genuinely conditional and not allowed. Art. 24.1 first paragraph: an emancipated Spaniard habitually resident abroad who voluntarily acquires another nationality loses Spanish nationality three years after that acquisition, unless within that period he declares to the Civil Registry his wish to retain it. Art. 23(b) requires an applicant acquiring Spanish nationality to renounce his previous one, excepting nationals of the same listed countries and Sephardim of Spanish origin. The BOE consolidation of art. 24 carries a note directing the reader to the Convenio de nacionalidad entre el Reino de España y la República Francesa (Montauban, 15 March 2021), ref. BOE-A-2022-4916, with implementing criteria at BOE-A-2022-5573, which adds France to the effective set by treaty rather than by amending the Code.

name: Ukraine
shape: designated-country list, inverted: loss only for nationalities outside the simplified-procedure list
instrument: Закон України «Про громадянство України» № 2235-III of 18 January 2001; arts. 5-1 and 19 as inserted and recast by Law No. 4502-IX of 18 June 2025; card states Редакція від 10.05.2026, підстава 4730-IX
quote_original: Наявність у громадянина України громадянства (підданства) іншої держави визнається у таких випадках
quote_translation: A Ukrainian citizen's holding of the citizenship of another state is recognised in the following cases
asymmetry_note: No birth-versus-naturalised split. The whole regime turns instead on WHICH other state: art. 19(1) restricts loss to voluntary acquisition of the citizenship of a state recognised by the Verkhovna Rada as an aggressor or occupier state, or of a state whose nationals cannot acquire Ukrainian citizenship by the simplified procedure.
subordinate_instrument: The list of states whose nationals may acquire Ukrainian citizenship by the simplified procedure, which is what art. 19(1) turns on, is set by the Cabinet of Ministers of Ukraine under art. 10-1, on a procedure the Cabinet itself approves. Art. 10-1 directs that EU membership and the application of restrictive measures against Russia in connection with the armed aggression be taken into account. This row will go stale by subordinate instrument without the Act changing, exactly as Pakistan's does by Gazette notification.
notes: One of the two highest-value findings in this batch. Ukraine sits on every restrictive list on the strength of the single-citizenship principle still in art. 2, but Law No. 4502-IX of 18 June 2025 inserted art. 5-1 and recast art. 19. Art. 5-1 recognises multiple citizenship in six defined cases: simultaneous acquisition at birth; acquisition by a Ukrainian child of the adopters' nationality; automatic acquisition on marriage; automatic acquisition on majority under foreign law where no confirming document was obtained; simplified-procedure acquisition under art. 10-1 by nationals of listed states; and acquisition by a Ukrainian citizen of the nationality of a listed state. Art. 19 further provides that the cases in art. 5-1(1)-(4) are not treated as voluntary acquisition at all. Any secondary source predating mid-2025 is a wrong answer that reads correctly. RETRIEVAL: the ordinary URL https://zakon.rada.gov.ua/laws/show/2235-14 serves the record card only, with a javascript-required notice and no article text. This is the metadata-only shape the brief warns about, and the /print suffix is the workaround.

name: Cuba
shape: none of the standard shapes: a non-exercise rule inside the territory, plus office-holding bars. Not automatic loss, not a permission regime, not a designated list.
instrument: Constitución de la República de Cuba, proclaimed 10 April 2019, published in Gaceta Oficial No. 5 Extraordinaria of 10 April 2019 (GOC-2019-406-EX5)
articles: art. 36; also arts. 33-35, 37-39; office-holding qualifications for President, Prime Minister and provincial Governor
quote_original: La adquisición de otra ciudadanía no implica la pérdida de
quote_translation: The acquisition of another citizenship does not entail the loss of [Cuban citizenship]
asymmetry_note: Yes, for public office only. The qualification "ser ciudadano cubano por nacimiento y no tener otra ciudadanía", to be a Cuban citizen by birth and hold no other citizenship, appears as a requirement for President, Prime Minister and provincial Governor. It does not affect the general citizenship rule in art. 36.
notes: The other highest-value finding in this batch, and the one where the common characterisation is wrong in the direction that costs a reader a decision. Cuba is routinely listed as prohibiting dual nationality; art. 36's first sentence says the opposite in terms. What Cuba actually operates is a non-exercise rule: the second sentence provides that Cuban citizens, while in the national territory, are governed by that condition on the terms established by law and may not make use of a foreign citizenship ("no pueden hacer uso de una ciudadanía extranjera"). Art. 38 provides that Cubans may not be deprived of their citizenship save on legally established grounds. quote_original is the line-safe form; the full sentence, which spans a PDF line break, reads "La adquisición de otra ciudadanía no implica la pérdida de la ciudadanía cubana." The art. 36 phrase "en los términos establecidos en la ley" points at an implementing citizenship law that was not reached, so the practical content of the non-exercise rule is not established, and the inbound direction is not established at all. Confidence is high for the constitutional text only.

name: Norway
shape: no restriction on holding a second nationality since 1 January 2020; separate absence-based loss at 22 that catches dual nationals born abroad
instrument: Lov om norsk statsborgerskap (statsborgerloven), LOV-2005-06-10-51, in force 1 September 2006; sec. 23 repealed by lov 20 des 2018 nr. 121, in force 1 January 2020; page states Sist endret LOV-2024-12-20-81
quote_original: taper sitt norske statsborgerskap når vedkommende fyller 22 år
quote_translation: loses his or her Norwegian citizenship on turning 22
asymmetry_note: Yes. Sec. 24 applies only to a person who acquired Norwegian citizenship AT BIRTH ("Den som ervervet norsk statsborgerskap ved fødselen") and who has not resided a total of two years in Norway, or a total of seven years in Norway and other Nordic countries. A naturalised Norwegian is outside it entirely. The loss extends to that person's children under sec. 24 fourth paragraph unless one parent remains Norwegian or the child independently meets the residence condition.
notes: Recorded as allowed because the operative restriction is gone: sec. 23, the provision that caused loss on acquiring another nationality, now reads only "(Opphevet)" with the annotation that it was repealed by lov 20 des 2018 nr. 121 in force 1 January 2020, and sec. 10, formerly the requirement to be released from another citizenship, has been repurposed as "Søkere med tilstrekkelig inntekt". The row exists for the positive rule in sec. 24, which is the one most likely to catch a Flag Paths reader who is a Norwegian dual national born abroad. It is an absence rule rather than a dual-nationality rule, and it is disapplied where the person would thereby become stateless; a person facing it may apply before turning 22 to keep citizenship on the ground of sufficient attachment to Norway. lovdata.no served the full text of this act without a paywall, so it is not the metadata-only trap on this instrument. Section-sign characters are absent from quote_original as a precaution.

name: Germany
shape: repeal of the loss-on-acquisition provision; no renunciation condition in the current naturalisation requirements
instrument: Staatsangehörigkeitsgesetz (StAG); sec. 25 repealed by the 2024 reform; page states Stand: Zuletzt geändert durch Art. 3 G v. 22.12.2025 I Nr. 364; 2026 I Nr. 49
articles: sec. 25 (repealed); sec. 10(1); sec. 26 (voluntary renunciation, permitted only where the person holds more than one nationality)
asymmetry_note: No birth-versus-naturalised split remains once sec. 25 is repealed.
notes: QUOTE CAUTION, read before verifying. The heading as displayed is "§ 25 (weggefallen)", but gesetze-im-internet HTML-escapes the section sign, so the string "§ 25 (weggefallen)" does NOT appear literally in the served bytes and will fail a byte-exact check. Only the parenthetical "(weggefallen)" appears literally, which is why it alone is given as quote_original; on its own it is not self-identifying, and a verifier must confirm it is the sec. 25 occurrence. The substantive fact is that sec. 25, the provision that caused loss of German citizenship on acquiring a foreign nationality, was repealed by the 2024 reform and now carries no text, and that sec. 10(1) as currently published contains no renunciation condition among the naturalisation requirements. A repeal is a fact about a real provision, which is why this is a row rather than a bare absence. Sec. 26 remains: a German may renounce citizenship only if he holds more than one nationality, and the declaration requires authority approval, refused to serving officials, judges, soldiers and those liable to military service subject to the exceptions in sec. 26(2).
